title: Croire et mettre : deux radicaux variables
summary: Build crois/croyons/croient and mets/mettons/mettent, then express a belief with penser que or croire que.
objectives: Conjugate croire and mettre and common mettre derivatives.
Use que to introduce what someone thinks or believes.

sections.title: Croire uses y only with nous and vous
paragraphs: Croire means believe or think. Its present has croi- in the singular and third-person plural, but croy- with nous and vous. Do not invent croyent for ils or elles. Croire quelqu'un means believe that person; croire que introduces a complete idea.
points: Croire: crois, crois, croit, croyons, croyez, croient.

examples.french:
Je **crois**
Tu **crois**
Il/elle/on **croit**
Nous **croyons**
Vous **croyez**
Ils/elles **croient**
examples.english:
I believe
You believe
He/she believes; one believes/we believe
We believe
You believe
They believe
examples.note: Y appears only in the nous and vous forms.
A person follows croire directly when we believe what they say.

mistakes.why: The third-person plural has i, not y.

sections.title: Keep que before the idea you believe
paragraphs: Penser que and croire que can both express think that or believe that. Penser focuses on an opinion or thought; croire presents a belief, sometimes with uncertainty, but the meanings overlap. Que introduces a clause: a group with its own subject and conjugated verb. English can omit that; French keeps que in this pattern. Que becomes qu' before a vowel or silent h.

Penser is a regular -er verb: je pense, tu penses, il/elle/on pense, nous pensons, vous pensez, ils/elles pensent. In these affirmative statements, use an ordinary indicative verb after que. More complex negative and doubtful uses belong to later lessons.
points: Je pense à Léa means I am thinking about Léa; je pense que Léa arrive means I think Léa is arriving.

examples.french: Je **pense que** le magasin est ouvert.
examples.english: I think the shop is open.
examples.note: Un magasin (m.) is a shop; que introduces the statement.

examples.english: She thinks he is arriving tomorrow.
I am thinking about my brother.
examples.note: À + person differs from que + a complete idea.

mistakes.why: French requires que, elided to qu' before il.

sections.title: Mettre has one t in the singular and two in the plural
paragraphs: Mettre means put and can mean put on clothing. Singular forms are mets, mets, met; the plural uses mett-. Remettre (put back/hand in/postpone), permettre (allow) and promettre (promise) follow the same pattern. A prefix stays attached to each form: je permets, tu permets, il/elle/on permet, nous permettons, vous permettez, ils/elles permettent. Likewise: je promets, tu promets, il/elle/on promet, nous promettons, vous promettez, ils/elles promettent.

Mettre is the action of putting clothing on; porter can describe wearing it. A noun object follows directly: mettre un manteau. This lesson teaches the present forms, not every possible meaning or complement of each derivative.
points: Un manteau (m.) = a coat; un dossier (m.) = a file.

examples.french:
Je **mets**
Tu **mets**
Il/elle/on **met**
Nous **mettons**
Vous **mettez**
Ils/elles **mettent**
examples.english:
I put
You put
He/she puts; one puts/we put
We put
You put
They put
I am putting on my coat.
examples.note: Mettre describes the action of dressing.

examples.french: Nous **remettons** les livres sur la table.
examples.english: We put the books back on the table.

examples.note: Promettre takes de before this infinitive; the singular has one t.

mistakes.why: Mettre has tt in every present plural form.

practice.prompt: Supply que with any required elision: 'Je pense ___ elle est ici.'

practice.explanation: Tu takes mets with one t.

practice.prompt: Choose the phrase meaning 'I am thinking about Paul'.
practice.explanation: À introduces a person; que requires a complete clause.

practice.prompt: Join with penser que, keeping je pense first: 'Je pense. Le bus arrive.'
answers: Je pense que le bus arrive.

practice.prompt: Supply penser: 'Nous ___ que tu as raison.'
Supply mettre: 'Vous ___ le dossier sur la table.'

practice.explanation: Promettre follows mettre with tt in the plural.

practice.prompt: Choose the sentence describing the action of putting a coat on.
practice.explanation: Mettre can mean put on clothing.

practice.prompt: Supply remettre: 'Nous ___ la chaise à sa place.'
Supply croire: 'On ___ que le train est en retard.'
Rewrite the whole sentence, adding only the missing link: 'Elle croit il travaille ici.'
practice.explanation: Croire que requires que, with elision before il.
The third-person singular is met, not mets.

production_task.prompt: Explain what you think about a meeting, then say what you put on the table to prepare. Use croire or penser with que and one plural form of mettre.
production_task.model_answer: Je pense que la réunion commence à dix heures. Nous mettons les documents sur la table.
production_task.translation: I think the meeting starts at ten o'clock. We put the documents on the table.
rubric: Keep que before the complete idea.
